accepted.s: The Sanjeevani digital health programme of Andhra Pradesh, commencing in August 2026, is primarily associated with which of the following?
o: Replacement of all public hospitals by private hospitals
Universal distribution of fortified food through fair-price shops
Free insurance cover of ₹5 lakh for every citizen
A digital health profile and ABHA ID for every citizen
accepted.x: Sanjeevani aims to create a digital health profile and ABHA ID for every citizen of Andhra Pradesh.
accepted.tq: Identify the defining feature of the programme rather than confusing it with an insurance scheme.
accepted.sec: AP healthcare interventions - telemedicine, Family Physician, village clinics, diagnostics

accepted.s:
Which of the following facilities and services are linked through the Sanjeevani digital health programme in Andhra Pradesh?
1. Primary Health Centres and hospitals
2. Laboratories and e-Aushadhi
3. 108 emergency services and 104 mobile medical units
4. Telemedicine and AI assistance
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Sanjeevani links PHCs, hospitals, laboratories, e-Aushadhi, 108 emergency services, 104 mobile medical units, telemedicine and AI assistance.
accepted.tq: Use the option containing all the listed components after checking each statement independently.
accepted.sec: AP healthcare interventions - telemedicine, Family Physician, village clinics, diagnostics

accepted.s: The Sanjeevani Citizen Wellness App is associated with which of the following programmes?
accepted.x: The Sanjeevani Citizen Wellness App is the citizen-facing application associated with the Sanjeevani digital health programme.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between similarly themed public-health initiatives by matching the application with its parent programme.
accepted.sec: AP healthcare interventions - telemedicine, Family Physician, village clinics, diagnostics

accepted.s: On 13 September 2026, which of the following was inaugurated in Andhra Pradesh under PM-ABHIM?
o: 10 Critical Care Blocks and 12 Integrated Public Health Laboratories
10 Health and Wellness Centres and 12 medical colleges
12 Critical Care Blocks and 10 Integrated Public Health Laboratories
accepted.x: Union Health Minister J. P. Nadda inaugurated 10 Critical Care Blocks and 12 Integrated Public Health Laboratories in Andhra Pradesh under PM-ABHIM.
accepted.tq: Match the two numerical components precisely instead of reversing their order.
accepted.sec: AP healthcare interventions - telemedicine, Family Physician, village clinics, diagnostics

accepted.s: The inauguration of the Critical Care Blocks and Integrated Public Health Laboratories under PM-ABHIM in Andhra Pradesh took place from:
accepted.x: The inauguration on 13 September 2026 was conducted from Vijayawada.
accepted.tq: Test the location separately from the date and numerical details of the same event.
accepted.sec: AP healthcare interventions - telemedicine, Family Physician, village clinics, diagnostics

accepted.s: The expenditure associated with the 10 Critical Care Blocks and 12 Integrated Public Health Laboratories inaugurated in Andhra Pradesh under PM-ABHIM was:
accepted.x: The infrastructure was inaugurated with an expenditure of ₹250 crore.
accepted.tq: Use a direct figure-based question to distinguish the stated allocation from nearby plausible amounts.
accepted.sec: AP healthcare interventions - telemedicine, Family Physician, village clinics, diagnostics

accepted.s: Andhra Pradesh’s Free Diagnostics Initiative is associated with which indicator?
accepted.x: The Free Diagnostics Initiative in Andhra Pradesh is associated with the CDI index.
accepted.tq: Separate a programme-specific abbreviation from health indicators such as IMR and TFR.
accepted.sec: AP healthcare interventions - telemedicine, Family Physician, village clinics, diagnostics

accepted.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Swachh Bharat Abhiyan — Sanitation and hygiene for disease prevention
2. Fit India Movement — Building fitness into daily life
3. Eat Right India — Safe, healthy and sustainable diets
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
accepted.x: All three pairs are correctly matched: Swachh Bharat focuses on sanitation, Fit India on daily fitness, and Eat Right India on safe, healthy and sustainable diets.
accepted.tq: Match each campaign with its precise objective before selecting the coded combination.
accepted.sec: Public health campaigns - Swachh Bharat, Fit India, Eat Right India

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
accepted.x: Swachh Bharat Abhiyan was launched in 2014, not 2018. Fit India is associated with 2019 and Eat Right India with 2018.
accepted.tq: Find the option that swaps the year of a campaign with another campaign’s year.
accepted.sec: Public health campaigns - Swachh Bharat, Fit India, Eat Right India

accepted.s: Eat Right India was created by which organisation, under which legislation?
o: FSSAI under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006
WHO under the National Health Policy, 2017
NITI Aayog under the Disaster Management Act, 2005
ICMR under the Indian Medical Council Act, 1956
accepted.x: Eat Right India is an initiative of the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India, established under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.
accepted.tq: Use the institution-and-legislation pairing to avoid swapping the responsible body with a health ministry or research body.
accepted.sec: Public health campaigns - Swachh Bharat, Fit India, Eat Right India

accepted.s: The Eat Right India and Fit India campaigns together seek to reduce deaths due to:
accepted.x: Together, Eat Right India and Fit India aim to reduce deaths caused by non-communicable diseases through healthier diets and increased physical activity.
accepted.tq: Infer the common public-health outcome from the two campaigns’ complementary objectives.
accepted.sec: Public health campaigns - Swachh Bharat, Fit India, Eat Right India

accepted.s: The Indian Research Fund Association, the predecessor of the Indian Council of Medical Research, was established in:
accepted.x: The Indian Research Fund Association was established in 1911 and was later renamed the ICMR in 1949.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the founding year from the later renaming year.
accepted.sec: ICMR - history and priorities

accepted.s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. ICMR was renamed from the Indian Research Fund Association
B. Indian Research Fund Association was established
C. World Health Organization was founded
D. Eat Right India was launched
Select the correct sequence.
accepted.x: The correct order is establishment of IRFA in 1911, WHO in 1948, renaming as ICMR in 1949, and Eat Right India in 2018.
accepted.tq: Fix the earliest and latest events first, then place the 1948 and 1949 events in sequence.
accepted.sec: ICMR - history and priorities

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes the relationship between the Indian Research Fund Association and ICMR?
o: ICMR was renamed as the Indian Research Fund Association in 1911.
The Indian Research Fund Association was renamed ICMR in 2017.
The Indian Research Fund Association was renamed ICMR in 1949.
Both were separate organisations established simultaneously in 1949.
accepted.x: The Indian Research Fund Association, established in 1911, was renamed the Indian Council of Medical Research in 1949.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between an organisation’s original name and its later institutional name.
accepted.sec: ICMR - history and priorities

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT a disease consortium or initiative listed in connection with the ICMR?
accepted.x: MERA India, the India TB Research Consortium and the India Hypertension Control Initiative are listed ICMR-related initiatives; India Food Security Consortium is not.
accepted.tq: Find the invented-looking member by comparing every option with the named ICMR initiatives.
accepted.sec: ICMR - history and priorities

accepted.s: MERA India, among the ICMR disease consortia, is associated with:
accepted.x: MERA India is the ICMR consortium associated with malaria.
accepted.tq: Test the exact disease association of a similarly structured consortium name.
accepted.sec: ICMR - history and priorities

accepted.s: The Medical Device and Diagnostic Mission Secretariat associated with ICMR seeks primarily to:
o: Increase dependence on imported medical devices
Reduce import dependence in medical devices and diagnostics
Replace all diagnostic laboratories with mobile units
accepted.x: The Secretariat aims to reduce India’s import dependence in medical devices and diagnostics.
accepted.tq: Identify the policy purpose from the stated institutional function rather than the institution’s name alone.
accepted.sec: ICMR - history and priorities

accepted.s: Which of the following is the correct chronological order of India’s National Health Policies?
accepted.x: India’s National Health Policies were issued in 1983, 2002 and 2017, in that order.
accepted.tq: Arrange policy years from earliest to latest, checking the middle year carefully.
accepted.sec: National Health Policy - years, NHP 2017 priorities and targets

accepted.s:
The National Health Policy, 2002, emphasised which of the following?
1. Increased public spending on health
2. A larger role for the private sector and NGOs
3. Exclusive provision of health services by the public sector
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: NHP 2002 called for increased public spending and a larger role for the private sector and NGOs. It did not advocate exclusive public-sector provision.
accepted.tq: Reject the absolute statement containing “exclusive” while retaining the two stated policy features.
accepted.sec: National Health Policy - years, NHP 2017 priorities and targets

accepted.s: Which of the following best characterises the approach of the National Health Policy, 2017?
o: A private-sector-only approach to emergency care
An assurance-based approach with comprehensive primary care
An insurance-only approach without public-sector services
A disease-specific approach limited to communicable diseases
accepted.x: NHP 2017 adopted an assurance-based approach and envisaged comprehensive primary care rather than an insurance-only or disease-specific model.
accepted.tq: Identify the official policy approach while rejecting extreme alternatives such as “only” and “private-sector-only.”
accepted.sec: National Health Policy - years, NHP 2017 priorities and targets

accepted.s:
Which of the following services form part of the comprehensive primary care package envisaged under NHP 2017?
1. Non-communicable disease care
2. Mental health care
3. Geriatric and palliative care
4. Free drugs, diagnostics and emergency care in public hospitals
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: NHP 2017 included NCD, mental health, geriatric and palliative care within comprehensive primary care, along with free drugs, diagnostics and emergency care in public hospitals.
accepted.tq: Check whether each service belongs to the broad primary-care package before selecting the complete combination.
accepted.sec: National Health Policy - years, NHP 2017 priorities and targets

accepted.s: Health and Wellness Centres are specifically associated with which of the following?
accepted.x: The establishment of Health and Wellness Centres is a priority associated with NHP 2017.
accepted.tq: Match the institutional priority with the correct policy year.
accepted.sec: National Health Policy - years, NHP 2017 priorities and targets

accepted.s: NHP 2017 set the target of raising public health expenditure to what proportion of GDP by 2025?
accepted.x: NHP 2017 targeted public health expenditure of 2.5% of GDP by 2025. The expenditure was 1.43% in 2022–23, indicating that the target had been missed at that point.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the policy target from the later reported achievement figure.
accepted.sec: National Health Policy - years, NHP 2017 priorities and targets

accepted.s:
Which of the following targets was associated with NHP 2017?
1. Life expectancy of 70 years by 2025
2. Total fertility rate of 2.1 by 2025
3. Infant mortality rate of 28 by 2019
4. Maternal mortality ratio of 100 by 2020
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: NHP 2017 targeted life expectancy of 70 years, TFR of 2.1, IMR of 28 and MMR of 100 within the specified target years.
accepted.tq: Read each target with its corresponding indicator and year before choosing the complete set.
accepted.sec: National Health Policy - years, NHP 2017 priorities and targets

accepted.s: The National Policy for Rare Diseases and the India Newborn Action Plan were issued in which years, respectively?
accepted.x: The National Policy for Rare Diseases was issued in 2021, while the India Newborn Action Plan dates to 2014.
accepted.tq: Use the “respectively” structure carefully to avoid reversing two close health-policy dates.
accepted.sec: National Health Policy - years, NHP 2017 priorities and targets

accepted.s: Which statement best expresses the criticism that an insurance-led public health policy may face?
o: It eliminates the need for public hospitals.
It increases coverage but may not ensure access.
It increases access without increasing coverage.
accepted.x: The criticism is that insurance-led policies can expand coverage while failing to ensure actual access to health services.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the related but different concepts of coverage and access.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: Which of the following statements is correct regarding the Andhra Pradesh Sanjeevani programme?
o: It is restricted to hospitalised patients in urban areas.
It is an ABDM-linked, citizen-wide digital health programme.
It deals exclusively with sanitation and hygiene.
It is limited to maintaining paper-based medical records.
accepted.x: Sanjeevani makes Andhra Pradesh an ABDM-linked, citizen-wide digital health state through digital profiles, ABHA IDs and connected health services.
accepted.tq: Apply the programme’s stated scope to distinguish a citizen-wide digital system from a narrow sectoral service.
accepted.sec: Universal angles
